analysis: The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md: it adds one table row (head line 527) documenting a new `--prompt-prep` benchmark mode with `--prompt-prep-lengths` and `--iterations`. The row says the mode is CPU-only, loads only the tokenizer, and times prompt preparation for chat, agent and tool-loop conversations. It prints JSON and exits 2 on any token-ID or decoded-field difference. The supplied units are base text only; the patch excerpt is the sole view of the change. The surrounding sections are unchanged. No security controls are altered: no changes to coordinator/provider WebSocket handling (TB-002), attestation/App Attest (TB-009, TB-011), key custody (A-003), or the prefix-cache storage and encryption described in T-041. The row does not mention prefix cache, inference, model weights, network access, or any secret/credential handling. The docs attribute the implementation to provider-swift/Sources/ProviderBenchmark/PromptPreparationBenchmark.swift. That source is not in this batch, so I could not check whether it handles synthetic prompts safely. It could write sensitive prompt content to logs or output. The doc states it prints JSON, so any real-prompt content in that output is an integration question for whoever reviews the Swift code. The doc row alone gives no evidence of a regression. Remaining question: whether the benchmark source, if included in the PR, avoids touching consumer data, the network, or persistent caches.
